newsitem.title: USA: Texaco profits gets extra boost from IRS refund.
newsitem.headline: Texaco profits gets extra boost from IRS refund.

text.p: Texaco Inc. posted sharply higher first-quarter profits Tuesday, thanks to a $488 million tax refund, part of a $700 million payback due from the Internal Revenue Service.
Shell Oil Co. said its profits climbed 7 percent to a record $517 million.
Texaco said it earned $980 million in the first three months of the year, or $3.72 a share vs. year-ago earnings of $386 million or $1.42 a year ago.

Excluding the IRS payment, which stems from a U.S. Supreme Court decision Monday not to review a lower court ruling, Texaco's earnings were $492 million, or $1.84 per share, topping Wall Street estimates.

The top court's denial of the government's appeal without comment or dissent, letting stand a U.S. appeals court ruling for Texaco in a case that dates back to the Saudi Arabian oil policy for 1979-81, added $1.88 a share to company's quarterly profits.
The White Plains, N.Y.-based company said it expected to receive a refund of more than $700 million as a result of the court's decision, mostly this year.
Texaco's stock jumped $1.50 to $105.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Texaco said it did well in the quarter, even without the big IRS refund.
"Our upstream business had another strong quarter, as higher commodity prices were enhanced by increased daily crude oil and natural gas production," said Texaco Chief Executive Peter Bijur.
He said the 27 percent rise in operating income was Texaco's 11th consecutive quarterly rise.

U.S. exploration and production earnings rose to $311 million from $267 million due to an average $3.11 rise in crude oil prices to $19.62 per barrel over the year ago quarter. Natural gas prices rose 51 cents to $2.66 per thousand cubic feet.

Texaco's international exploration and production profits rose to $156 million from $130 million a year ago. International refining and marketing earnings rose to $104 million from $92 million a year ago.

U.S. refining and marketing's earnings were subdued at $6.0 million vs. $4.0 million. Texaco said that its U.S. operations were hurt by refinery fires late in 1996 and early 1997 and by weak West Coast profit margins.

Texaco recently signed a preliminary agreement with Royal Dutch/Shell Transport & Trading to combine their U.S. refining and marketing operations, which should be in place by 1998 and will result in substantial savings.
Shell Oil, the U.S. unit of Royal/Dutch Shell Group, said it earned $517 million in the first quarter vs. year ago earnings of $483 million.
The Houston-based oil giant said revenues rose to $7.63 billion from $6.36 billion.
"We are pleased with such a good start in 1997," said President Philip Carroll.
"Operations continued to improve, with increased domestic crude oil production over the same period in 1996, as well as continued growth in both oil and chemical products sales volumes," he said.

Overall, income in the quarter benefited from higher crude oil and natural gas prices and increased refined products and chemical sales volumes. But the gain was partially offset by lower refined product margins.
Shell operating profits from its oil products unit fell $59 million to $12 million in the first quarter of 1997.
